title: Adaptive cycle tranche & staffing guidelines for capacity-constrained cycles
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Define a pragmatic, repeatable framework for slicing a product cycle into tranches with explicit staffing lanes (baseline, surge, critical path) and deterministic scope-cut rules to preserve OKR delivery when capacity is constrained. Goals: 1) Reduce ad-hoc scope churn during triage and ensure predictable commitments to stakeholders; 2) Give engineering managers clear rules for when to allocate surge capacity, pull from backlog, or cut scope; 3) Provide PMs with a transparent escalation path and measurable signals for triggering tranche promotions/cuts. Intended users: PMs, Eng Managers, Design leads, GTM stakeholders. Problem statement: Recent cycles had ~18% scope creep and several late-cycle rollbacks due to ambiguous surge criteria and no automated enforcement for low-quality backlog items. We need a light-weight operational playbook (not a heavy process) that can scale across multiple product teams and support both Hosted/Dedicated/Private product lines. Key components: - Tranche definitions: Baseline (committed work sized to historical throughput), Surge (small scoped wins for high-impact/blocked items), Critical Path (OKR-linked items with strict fallbacks). - Staffing lanes: baseline lane (normal headcount), surge lane (pre-approved pool: 10% of squad FTEs by default), float lane (rotating cross-functional engineers to handle incidents). - Promotion rules: explicit signals (error budget burn > X, blockers > Y, customer escalation flagged as high) to move a work item into Surge lane. - Automated scope-cut rules: lowest execution confidence, smallest ROI, last-in backlog get deferred unless tagged OKR-critical. - Rollout & enforcement: cycle planning checklist, a dedicated "Cycle Triage" Slack channel, and triage cadence (mid-cycle review + final freeze). Acceptance criteria: 1) Playbook adopted by at least 3 product squads in next cycle; 2) Surge pool allocations visible in CycleOps dashboard; 3) Triaging process reduces unplanned rollbacks by 50% in next 2 cycles. Artifacts: draft playbook in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CycleOps/Adaptive+Tranche+Guidelines, draft policy PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/214, example triage dashboard: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/cycleops/tranches. Out-of-scope: long-term hiring plans and org-level headcount decisions (this is an operational allocation playbook for the next 3 cycles).
